name: 2019 05 01 May PC Agenda Packet
agenda_text:
CITY OF ING LEWOOD
  ECONOMIC AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DEPARTMENT
  PLANNING COMMISSION
  MEETING AGENDA
May 1, 2019 7:00 P.M.
Community Room – First Floor
1 West Manchester Boulevard
----------------------------------------------------------------------

1.  Pledge of Allegiance.

2.  Roll Call.

3.  Communications from staff.

4.  Public Comments Regarding Agenda Items. Persons wishing to
  address the Planning Commission on any item on the agenda other
  than a public hearing may do so at this time.

5.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  a. A public hearing to consider an application by Douglas M.
  Champion representing East Beach Inglewood, LLC for Zone Change
  No. 2018-001 (ZC-2018-001) to allow a zone change of an
  approximately 67,487 square-foot (1.55 acres) site from R-2
  (Limited-Multiple  family  Residential)  and  M-1  (Light
  Manufacturing) to R-4 (Multiple-family Residential) at 355 La
  Colina Drive and 338 to 358 East Beach Avenue (AIN 4015-017-
  003; 017 and 025).

  1. Preliminary Recommendations:
  a. Preliminary CEQA Recommendations: Affirm Addendum to
  Environmental Impact Report EA-EIR-2016-044
  b. Preliminary Recommendations: Adopt Findings and the
  attached resolution approving ZC-2018-001 subject to
  conditions.

  b. A public hearing to consider an application by Lynne Weaver,
  representing Three Weavers Brewing Company, for Special Use
  Permit No. 2019-002 (SP-2019-002) to amend Condition No. 5 and
  6 of Planning Commission Resolution No. 1699 for Special Use
  Permit No. 1193 (SP-1193) for an existing brewery and tasting
  room on a 2.99 acre C-3 and M-1 (Heavy Commercial and Light
  Manufacturing) zoned property at 1031 W. Manchester Boulevard.

  1. Preliminary Recommendations:
  a. Preliminary CEQA Recommendations: Affirm Notice of
  Exemption EA-CE-2019-010
  b. Preliminary Recommendations: Adopt Findings and the
  attached resolution approving SP-2019-002 subject to
  conditions.

  c. A public hearing to consider an application by Jakim Stewart,
  representing Drobe Stogies, for Special Use Permit No. 2019-003
  (SP-2019-003) to allow on-site consumption of alcoholic
  beverages within an existing cigar lounge on a 3,300 square-
  foot, C-2 (General Commercial) zoned property at 1322 North La
  Brea Avenue.

  1. Preliminary Recommendations:
  a. Preliminary CEQA Recommendations: Affirm Notice of
  Exemption EA-CE-2018-088
  b. Preliminary Recommendations: Adopt Findings and the
  attached resolution approving SP-2019-003 subject to
  conditions.

  1
 6.  NON PUBLIC HEARINGS

  a. A non-public hearing to allow two murals on the exterior of an
  existing approximately 4,037 square-foot tenant space within an
  existing 4,619 square-foot commercial building on a 4,650
  square-foot property at 170 N. La Brea Avenue (AIN 4021-008-
  009).

  1. Preliminary Recommendations:
  a. Preliminary CEQA Recommendations: Affirm Notice of
  Exemption EA-CE-2019-035
  b. Preliminary Recommendations: Adopt Findings and the
  attached resolution approving DR-2019-003 subject to
  conditions.

7.  Commission Initiatives

8.  Public Comments. Anyone wishing to address the Planning
  Commission on any matter within their jurisdiction and not
  elsewhere considered on the agenda may do so at this time.

9.  Adjournment.

If you will require special accommodations, due to a disability,
please contact the Planning Division at (310) 412-5230 or FAX (310)
412-5681, One Manchester Boulevard, Fourth Floor, Inglewood City Hall,
Inglewood, CA 90301. All requests for special accommodations must be
received 48 hours prior to the day of the hearing(s).

"Si no entiende esta noticia o si necesita más información, favor de
llamar a este número (310) 412-5230."

In the event that the Planning Commission meeting of May 1, 2019 is
not held, or is concluded prior to a public hearing or other agenda
item being considered, the public hearing or non-public hearing agenda
item will automatically be continued to the next regular Planning
Commission meeting.

MINUTES
  INGLEWOOD PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  WEDNESDAY, MAY 1, 2019
(1) PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:
The City of Inglewood Planning Commission held its Planning
Commission meeting on Wednesday, May 1, 2019, in the Community
Room, on the first floor, in City Hall. Following the Pledge of
Allegiance by Commissioner Rice, the meeting was called to order
at 7:01 p.m.

(2) ROLL CALL:
Present:  Commissioner Erick Holly
  Commissioner David Rice
  Chairman Larry Spring

Excused
Absence:  Commissioner Aide’ Trejo
  Commissioner Terry Coleman

Staff:  Mindy Wilcox, AICP, Planning Manager
  Jeff Lewis, Assistant City Attorney
  Eddy Ikemefuna, Senior Planner
  Fred Jackson, Senior Planner
  Bernard McCrumby, Planner
  Marissa Fewell, Assistant Planner
  Christopher E. Jackson, Sr., Director of E.C.D.
  Evangeline Lane, Secretary

(3) STAFF COMMUNICATIONS:
Ms. Wilcox stated that Item 5a is being pulled from tonight’s
Planning Commission’s meeting, and continued to June 5, 2019 per
the applicant’s request and the applicant is present. Item 5c has
a revised resolution for the public which is located at the sign-
in entry table as well as for the planning commission which has
been placed at your stations and also the staff report has been
modified. Last, she received an email for an Excused Absence from
Commissioner Terry Coleman.

(4) PUBLIC COMMENTS:

Eld. S. L. Garrett and Rev. William Garrett questioned why the
postponement of item 5a?

Chairman Springs replied that Item 5A was continued per the request
of the applicant, who is present this evening.

(5) PUBLIC HEARING:

5A. ZONE CHANGE NO. 2018-001(ZC-2018-001) AT 355 LA COLINA DRIVE
AND 338 – 358 EAST BEACH AVENUE. A public hearing to consider an
application by Douglas M. Champion representing East Beach
Inglewood, LLC for Zone Change No. 2018-001 (ZC-2018-001) to allow
a zone change of an approximately 67,487 square-foot (1.55 acres)
site from R-2 (Limited-Multiple family Residential) and M-1 (Light
Manufacturing) to R-4 (Multiple-family Residential) at 355 La
Colina Drive and 338 to 358 East Beach Avenue (AIN 4015-017-003;
017 and 025).

Chairman Springs asked for a motion to continue Item 5A, per the
request of the applicant to next month’s June 5, 2019, regular
Planning Commission meeting.
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
May 1, 2019
MOTION:

Commissioner Holly made the motion to Continue Item 5A to regular
Planning Commission Meeting, June 5, 2019, along with re-noticing
and was seconded by Commissioner Rice.

The motion passed by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners Holly, Rice, and Chairman Springs.

5B. SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2019-002 (SP-2019-002) AT 1031 WEST
MANCHESTER BOULEVARD. A public hearing to consider an application
by Lynne Weaver, representing Three Weavers Brewing Company, for
Special Use Permit No. 2019-002 (SP-2019-002) to amend Conditions
No. 5 and 6 of Planning Commission Resolution No. 1699 for Special
Use Permit No. 1193 (SP-1193) for an existing brewery and tasting
room on a 2.99 acre C-3 and M-1 (Heavy Commercial and Light
Manufacturing) zoned property at 1031 W. Manchester Boulevard.

Ms. Marissa Fewell, Assistant Planner made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Rice asked
  - For an explanation of Conditions No. 5 and No. 6
  Ms. Fewell explained that there were a couple of typographical
  errors which were included in the planning commissioner’s
  packet, and on page 2, the typos were highlighted. Condition
  No. 5 dealt with the actual square footage of the outdoor dining
  and Condition No. 6 deals with the hours of operation.

  -  The hours of operation are now going to be extended due to
  the dining there?
  Ms. Fewell stated yes, that is correct.

  -  Since there should be by right a restaurant for the applicants
  use, so why the Special Use Permit requirement?
  Ms. Fewell stated because of the outdoor dining.

  -  Would the outdoor dining require the Special Use Permit
  because of the distribution of alcohol?
  Ms. Fewell stated that the outdoor dining alone is requiring a
  Special Use Permit and the original approval was for 300 square
  feet and this design has a larger outdoor dining area adds 2900
  square feet.

Chairman Springs asked the applicant to come forward to address
the planning commission and speak about their project.

Ms. Lynn Weaver, Owner and operator of Three Weavers Brewery.

Chairman Springs asked if there was anyone For or Against the
project to come forward.

FOR: / AGAINST:

Stuart Bailey, Inglewood Resident
  - Asked on behalf the absent Commissioner Coleman if there could
  be more cameras added to the site for health and safety.
  - Also add several live Security Officers to show physical
  strength and protection.

  2
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
May 1, 2019
Chairman Springs asked for closing comments and also a motion from
the Planning Commission.

MOTION:

Commissioner Holly made the motion to affirm the notice of
exemption EA-CE-2019-010 and adopt the attached resolution
approving SP-2019-002 with 17 conditions and was second by
Commissioner Rice, Resolution No. 1833,

  A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE
  CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING A
  CERTAIN SPECIAL USE PERMIT TO LYNNE WEAVER,
  REPRESENTING THREE WEAVERS BREWING COMPANY TO
  AMEND CONDITION NO. 5 AND 6 OF PLANNING
  COMMISSION RESOLUTION NO. 1699 FOR SPECIAL USE
  PERMIT NO. 1193 (SP-1193) FOR AN EXISTING
  BREWERY AND TASTING ROOM ON A 2.99 ACRE C-3
  AND  M-1  (HEAVY  COMMERCIAL  AND  LIGHT
  MANUFACTURING) ZONED PROPERTY AT 1031 WEST
  MANCHESTER BOULEVARD

The motion passed by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners Holly, Rice, and Chairman Springs

Ms. Wilcox explained the appeals process.

5C. SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2019-003 (SP-2019-003) AT 1322 NORTH LA
BREA AVENUE. A public hearing to consider an application by Jakim
Stewart, representing Drobe Stogies, for Special Use Permit No.
2019-003 (SP-2019-003) to allow on-site consumption of alcoholic
beverages within an existing cigar lounge on a 3,300 square-foot,
C-2 (General Commercial) zoned property at 1322 North La Brea
Avenue.

Ms. Marissa Fewell, Assistant Planner made the staff presentation.

Chairman Larry Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were
any questions for staff. There were none. Asked the applicant to
come forward and address the planning commission.

Mr. Jakim Stewart, owner of Drobe Stogies
Mr. Ryan Taylor, co-owner of Drobe Stogies

Chairman Springs opened the floor for questions to the applicant
by the planning commission.

Commissioner Rice asked the applicant, Mr. Taylor:
  - About the food that will be provided for purchase by the
  patrons.
  Mr. Taylor stated that at the present, there is no set menu
  ready, but there will be pre-packaged sandwiches available for
  purchase starting at $8.00/per, consisting from Roast Beef to
  Turkey sandwiches and housed in their refrigeration system until
  purchased.

Chairman Springs asked:
  - What or how does the ventilation system work in a cigar
  lounge and would anyone leaving the lounge smell like cigar
  smoke?
  Mr. Taylor stated that it is a possibility that upon leaving
  your will carry the smell of cigar smoke out with you, but that
  3
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
May 1, 2019
  their lounge has the latest and strongest ventilation system
  that should cut down to a bare minimum the smell of cigar on
  your clothing. There has been a heavy price paid for a four ton
  unit that pulls the smoke out of the lounge instantly and that
  there is no smoky lounge environment when you step into the
  lounge.

Chairman Springs also asked:
  - About the cost of membership?
  Mr. Taylor stated that membership for one year is $1500.00,
  which includes a locker, where the patron will receive a custom
  made jacket (since he designs men’s suits) and the member can
  hang up their personal suit jacket, which will be filtered from
  smoke along with bringing their own cigars. There are multiple
  levels available and the next level is $750.00, per year where
  the member will receive a custom designed shirt and a smaller
  locker. Next the last level at $350.00 does not receive a locker,
  but you can still enjoy the benefits of membership which
  includes 10% off of purchases, there are sometimes a gathering
  of “members only” evenings, there is live entertainment at times
  that members can enjoy.

Chairman Springs asked:
  - What about Senior Citizen or Military discounts?
  Mr. Taylor stated “Yes, there is a Military discount”.

FOR: / AGAINST:

Stuart Bailey, Inglewood Resident
  - Just a concerned citizen
  - Will there be women invited to the club?
  - Can the members smoke marijuana in the club?
  - Is there enough security so that the lounge is not robbed,
  due to all of the money these members appear to have, but all
  is well.

Chairman Springs asked for closing comments and also a motion from
the Planning Commission.

Commissioner Holly stated that Cigar Lounges are open to both men
and women, you cannot smoke anything in a cigar lounge but a cigar,
no cigarettes or any other substance... just a cigar.

MOTION:

Commissioner Rice made the motion to affirm the categorical
exemption EA-CE-2018-088 and adopt the attached resolution
approving SP-2019-003, subject to 13 conditions and was seconded
by Commissioner Holly, Resolution No. 1834,

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY PLANNING COMMISSION
  OF  THE  CITY  OF  INGLEWOOD,  CALIFORNIA,
  APPROVING A CERTAIN SPECAIL USE PERMIT JAKIM
  STEWART, REPRESENTING DROBE STOGIES, TO ALLOW
  ON-SITE CONSUMPTION OF ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES
  WITHIN AN EXISTING CIGAR LOUNGE ON A 3,300
  SQUARE-FOOT, C-2 (GENERAL COMMERCIAL) ZONED
  PROPERTY LOCATED AT 1322 NORTH LA BREA AVENUE

The motion passed by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners Holly, Rice, and Chairman Springs

Ms. Wilcox explained the appeals process.

May 1, 2019
(6)  NON-PUBLIC HEARINGS

6A. DESIGN REVIEW NO. 2019-003 (DR-2019-003) AT 170 NORTH LA BREA
AVENUE. A non-public hearing to allow two murals on the exterior
of an existing approximately 4,037 square-foot tenant space within
an existing 4,619 square-foot commercial building on a 4,650
square-foot property at 170 N. La Brea Avenue (AIN 4021-008-009).

Ms. Taylor Kay, Assistant Planner, made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Holly asked about:
  - The only difference with regards to murals and signs is the
  applicant is requesting to have two signs, where the code
  allows only one?
  Ms. Kay stated “Yes”, where the code allows one and the applicant
  is requesting two.

Commissioner Rice asked:
  - Asked the purpose for the Design Review for this applicant?
  Ms. Kay stated that the Design Review would be merely for the
  aesthetics and the Sign Adjustment would be for increasing the
  number.
  - Color of the building, what is the color scheme?
  Ms. Kay stated the color will be grey exterior and the interior
  will have both grey and black, at present the subject site is
  tan.

Chairman Springs asked for the applicant to come forward and address
the planning commission.

Mr. Brion Moran, Architect and applicant,
Mr. A.J. Relan, Co-Owner of L.A.’s Hilltop Coffee and Kitchen
Mr. Yunnie Hagos, Co-Owner of L.A.’s Hilltop Coffee and Kitchen

Mr. Relan stated that they presently have one shop in the Los
Angeles area known as Windsor Hills, and they are looking to expand
their shop into the Inglewood area. They will hire local residents
once opened, at a fair minimum wage.

Chairman Springs asked the planning commission if they have any
questions for the applicants?

Commissioner Rice asked about:
  - If the present Los Angeles location is staffed with local
  hires?
  Mr. Relan stated “Yes, that is correct”.

Chairman Springs asked for a motion from the Planning Commission.

MOTION:

Commissioner Holly made the motion to affirm the categorical
exemption EA-CE-2019-035 and adopt the attached resolution
approving DR-2019-003 subject to the 14 conditions and was second
by Commissioner Rice, Resolution No. 1835,

Ms. Wilcox explained the appeals process.

(7)  PUBLIC COMMENTS:

Mr. Asghar Tootlan, 823 Java Avenue, #9, Inglewood Resident and
HOA President and Representative.
  - Issues with the $5.00 Car Wash on the corner of Arbor Vitae
  and La Brea Avenue, on the North-East corner.
  - Patrons of the car wash constantly park in the alley which
  blocks the garages of the tenants of the Java Apartments,
  as their building abuts the alley.
  - The car wash is running water all through the alley and the
  smell is very bad.
  - The patrons once they have finished getting their cars
  washed, exit through the alley and dump their trash outside
  of their car onto the alley floor.
  - Patrons constantly park their vehicles in the alley which
  prevents the tenants of the Java Apartments from entering
  their garages and the patrons refuse to move.
  - Mr. Tootlan stated he has spent over two years on the
  telephone trying to get someone to listen to his request on
  behalf of the tenants at the Java Apartments and finally he
  was able to speak with Mr. Eddy Ikemefuna of Planning who
  suggested he attend the Planning Commission meeting this
  evening to bring to the attention of the planning commission
  and upper management.

Chairman Springs asked Ms. Wilcox if she could assist with Mr.
Tootlan’s dilemma and Ms. Wilcox stated that she will get with Mr.
Eddy Ikemefuna to confirm some information and look into the
situation along with contacting Code Enforcement to assist and
possibly settle the situation.

(8) COMMISSION INITIATIVES:

Commissioner Holly no initiatives,  just  wanted  to  thank  the
community for coming out.

Commissioner Rice welcome to Inglewood.

Chairman Springs wanted to thank Mr. Christopher Jackson for giving
an excellent presentation to his board with information. Thank you
to Ms. Wilcox in setting up the tour for the planning commission
next week on May 6, 2019, it is very much appreciated.
